A day for each feast

Twelfth Night

Twelfth Night Celebration at Home

Celebrate the close of Christmastide with a day of joyful traditions, festive feasting, and lively merriment rooted in medieval European customs.

  1. Morning

    Prepare Festive Foods

    Begin the day by baking a king cake filled with almonds and preparing figgy pudding to honor the traditional Twelfth Night feast.

    Recipes: King Cake · Figgy Pudding

  2. Midday

    Roast the Meats

    Cook a hearty roasted meat to share with family and friends, symbolizing abundance before the Epiphany fast begins.

    Recipes: Traditional Twelfth Night Roasted Meat

  3. Afternoon

    Mix Spiced Ale

    Brew or prepare spiced ale to enjoy throughout the evening, embodying the festive spirit of the season.

    Recipes: Traditional Spiced Ale

  4. Late Afternoon

    Crown the Twelfth Night King or Queen

    Hide a bean charm in the king cake and crown the person who finds it as the Twelfth Night monarch, continuing the medieval tradition.

    Recipes: King Cake

  5. Early Evening

    Wassailing and Singing

    Gather at doorways to sing wassail songs, spreading cheer and goodwill to neighbors as was customary during Twelfth Night.

  6. Evening

    Feast Together

    Share the roasted meats, figgy pudding, and spiced ale in a communal feast, celebrating the end of the Christmas season.

    Recipes: Traditional Twelfth Night Roasted Meat · Figgy Pudding · Traditional Spiced Ale

  7. Night

    Dismantle Holiday Greenery

    Carefully take down the Christmas greenery to avoid bad luck in the coming year, marking the close of the festival.

End the day reflecting on the season's joys as you prepare for the Epiphany fast ahead.
